threads.body: [General] This selector also creates `testSpring3StableSemconv`, but `src/testSpring3` contains only web MVC and RestClient autoconfiguration tests; it does not exercise database instrumentation or assert database attributes. The database opt-in cannot affect that suite, so this adds a redundant test run contrary to the semantic-relevance criterion. Restrict the match to the default, Spring 2, and Spring 4 suites.

replies.body:
Addressed in 225c6e98a822956ddb84638bb7581980c2e764f2.

Analysis: All three selectors were mapping the full JvmTestSuite container without filtering to suites that actually exercise the semconv being opted in. In spring-boot-autoconfigure, `testSpring3` has no database instrumentation tests, so the database opt-in has no effect there. In logback-appender, only `test` and `slf4j2ApiTest` have `captureCodeAttributes` enabled in their logback-test.xml; the other three suites never emit code attributes regardless of the `code` opt-in. In apache-dubbo, `testClusterInvoker` tests only wrapper contract and registry-address propagation and produces no telemetry, so the `rpc` opt-in cannot affect it. Each fix narrows the suite selector to the suites that actually assert the semconv being varied.

Upsides: Eliminates redundant test task registrations and CI runs for suites where the semconv opt-in has no observable effect, reducing CI time and avoiding misleading green results from no-op variants.

Downsides: No material downside identified.

threads.body: [General] Mapping every suite adds stable and duplicate-mode runs for `asyncAppenderTest`, `logstashMarkerTest`, and `logstashStructuredArgsTest`, but those suites' appender configurations do not enable `captureCodeAttributes`; only the default and `slf4j2ApiTest` suites exercise code semconv. These six runs therefore cannot add semconv coverage. Filter the collection to the two relevant suites.
